_national.labelling: NTA labelling standard (Notice No. 18 of October 2015, applied from 30 October 2018): "Nihon wine" (Japan Wine) means wine made in Japan from 100% Japanese-grown grapes, and only Japan Wine may name a place, variety or vintage. Place: a vineyard-origin name needs 85% of grapes from it; a winery-location name must say it is where the wine was made; a plain place name (e.g. "Osaka") needs both 85% of grapes and the winery there. Variety 85% (up to three may be named; with three, percentages shown and the named varieties must total 85%); vintage 85%. Domestic wines using imported concentrate or bulk wine must say so on the front label and may not show place, variety or vintage.
_national.other: Five wine GIs protected by the NTA, each covering a whole prefecture: Yamanashi (2013), Hokkaido (2018), Yamagata, Osaka and Nagano (2021). Each GI requires 100% local grapes from a listed set of varieties (vinifera, labrusca, hybrids and Japanese crosses), Japan Wine status, no water, alcohol or spirits, limits on chaptalisation and acid adjustment, and storage and bottling in the prefecture, all checked by a control body.

jp-hokkaido.varieties: Listed vinifera (Kerner, Zweigelt, Pinot Noir, Müller-Thurgau, Bacchus and others), labrusca (Niagara, Campbell Early and others), wild Vitis (Amurensis, Coignetiae) and hybrids (Yamasachi, Seibel 13053 and others).
jp-hokkaido.min_alcohol: Juice sugar at least 16% for vinifera, 13% for labrusca, 15% for wild and hybrid varieties (1 point lower in a bad year). Wine at most 14.5% abv; total acidity floors of 4.8 to 5.8 g/l depending on colour and ripeness. Added sugar may not exceed the grapes' own sugar; acidification essentially barred (max 1 g/l only for very ripe grapes).
jp-hokkaido.labelling: GI since 28 June 2018. 100% Hokkaido grapes; made, stored and bottled in Hokkaido.

jp-nagano.varieties: Listed vinifera in groups (A: Merlot, Chardonnay; B: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc and others), labrusca (Seibel 13053, Delaware, Concord, Niagara) and Japanese crosses (Asama Merlot, Shinano Riesling and others).
jp-nagano.min_alcohol: Two tiers. Nagano Wine: juice sugar from 15 to 17% by group; 7.5% to under 20% abv (under 15% if chaptalised). Nagano Wine Premium: higher sugar (e.g. 19% for Merlot and Chardonnay), at least 8% abv, sugar only as sucrose, no brandy, total SO2 max 250 mg/l, still wines only. Chaptalisation capped per variety group (e.g. 7 g/100 ml for group A vinifera, 5 g for Premium).
jp-nagano.labelling: GI since 30 June 2021, building on the Nagano Appellation Control system started in 2002. 100% Nagano grapes; made, stored and bottled in Nagano; no water.

jp-osaka.varieties: Table-grape varieties Delaware, Koshu, Muscat Bailey A, Kyoho, Pione, plus listed wine varieties (Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Campbell Early and others).
jp-osaka.min_alcohol: Juice sugar at least 16% (Delaware 18%, Koshu 14%, early-picked Delaware 12%). Wine at least 9% abv (sweet wines 4.5%).
jp-osaka.labelling: GI since 30 June 2021. 100% Osaka grapes; made, stored and bottled in the prefecture; acidification max 1 g/l.

jp-yamagata.varieties: Listed vinifera (Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and others), labrusca (Delaware, Niagara, Campbell Early, Concord, Steuben) and others (Muscat Bailey A, Koshu, Shine Muscat and more).
jp-yamagata.min_alcohol: Juice sugar at least 16% for vinifera, 12% for labrusca, 14% for others. Wine 7% to under 20% (under 15% if chaptalised). Added sugar may not exceed the grapes' own sugar; acid additions max 6 g/l.
jp-yamagata.labelling: GI since 30 June 2021. 100% Yamagata grapes; made, stored and bottled in the prefecture.

jp-yamanashi.varieties: Koshu, Muscat Bailey A, Black Queen, Bailey Alicante A, Delaware, listed hybrids (Kai Noir, Kai Blanc, Sun-Semillon and others) and 30 vinifera varieties (Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and others).
jp-yamanashi.min_alcohol: Grape juice sugar at least 14% for Koshu, 18% for vinifera, 16% for others (1 point lower in a declared bad year; lower for bottle-fermented sparkling). Wine 8.5% to under 20% (under 15% if chaptalised; sweet wines over 45 g/l from 4.5%). Added sugar max 10 g/100 ml for 100% Koshu, 6 g for wines over 85% vinifera, 8 g for others.
jp-yamanashi.labelling: First Japanese wine GI (16 July 2013). 100% Yamanashi grapes, made, stored and bottled in Yamanashi; acidification max 9 g/l; total SO2 max 250 mg/l (dry wines). Certified by the Yamanashi GI management commission.
